title: Short Stuff: The Church Choir That Didn't Explode
summary: Short Stuff episode on the 1950 Beatrice, Nebraska church explosion at West Side Baptist church. A gas leak ignited by Reverend Walter Clempole's furnace lighting destroyed the church on March 1, 1950, five minutes after the 7:00 pm... (choir practice was scheduled for 7:20 pm), yet none of the fifteen choir members was inside because each arrived late for individual reasons: a dirty dress needing replacement, a geometry problem, a car breakdown, a missed-shoes errand, a letter, lethargy, a nap, a radio program, and babysitting. The hosts describe the odds as roughly one in a million, and cite Life magazine and Snopes as sources.

segments.title: Intro and setup of the coincidence
segments.summary: Josh introduces the story as one of history's most astounding coincidences: a church blew up in Beatrice, Nebraska on the evening of March 1, 1950, yet no choir member was inside because all were late.

segments.title: The explosion and the gas leak
segments.summary: The hosts describe the blast that destroyed West Side Baptist Church, believed to be a gas leak ignited by the furnace Reverend Walter Clempole lit before choir practice, after which he went home for dinner.

segments.title: Timing and odds
segments.summary: Choir practice started at 7:20 pm on Wednesdays, and the explosion came at 7 pm, five minutes after practice officially started. None of the fifteen choir members was present. Based on past lateness, the odds were about one in a million, comparable to being struck by lightning.

segments.title: Reasons for lateness: Clempole family and Vander Grift
segments.summary: Reverend Clempole usually arrived about 7:10 pm, but his daughter's dirty dress meant his wife had to iron a new one, making the family late. LaDonna Vander Grift was finishing a geometry problem when Rhoena and Sadie Sts sisters called for a ride after their car broke down, so she was also delayed.

segments.title: Other members' excuses
segments.summary: Leonard Schuster's mother's shoes delayed her; Herbert Kith was writing a letter; Joyce Black admitted she was feeling lazy in the cold; Marilyn Paul fell asleep after turkey dinner and was woken late by her mother, the choir director; Lucille Jones was listening to a radio program while Dorothy waited.

segments.title: Harvey and wrap-up
segments.summary: Harvey was babysitting his kids while his wife was out of town and lost track of time while talking. The hosts note that the church believed God led them away, and credit Life magazine and Snopes for sourcing.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck thank their sources, the producer, and listeners, and close the short episode.
